The '''Greater Tion''' was a region of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] that surrounded the [[Tion Cluster/Legends|Tion Cluster]] and exhibited [[Tionese (group)/Legends|Tionese]] influence. This historical designation was used after the area was unified by [[Xim/Legends|Xim the Despot]] circa [[25,000 BBY/Legends|25,000 BBY]] and during the next millennium until this isolated region of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] joined the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]].

==Geography==
[[File:Tion_History.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The history of the Greater Tion.]]
Following the region's annexation in [[23,900 BBY]] by the Galactic Republic, the Greater Tion was divided into a number of [[Sector/Legends|sectors]]. The [[Tion Cluster/Legends|Tion Cluster]] itself eventually became organized into the [[Tion Hegemony/Legends|Tion Hegemony]] and the [[Kingdom of Cron]] by the time of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], and became a hotbed of [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatism]]. In retaliation, the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] split the Hegemony into the [[Allied Tion sector/Legends|Allied Tion sector]] and the Tion Hegemony, while renaming the Kingdom of Cron the [[Cronese Mandate/Legends|Cronese Mandate]]. The [[Cronese]] were typically more outward-looking than the rest of the Cluster, and the Allied Tion, though it lacked a historical identity, became known for its manufacturing and trade. The rump of the Tion Hegemony, however, became divided into two very different regions: the mildly-wealthy [[Livien League|Livien Worlds]] at the head of the [[Desevran Trace]] near the [[Perlemian Trade Route/Legends|Perlemian Trade Route]], and the poor, culturally-different worlds beyond the [[Indrexu Spiral]] along the [[Tion Trade Route]], known as the [[Back Spiral]].

The Empire reorganized the regions surrounding the Cluster as well, carving the [[Indrexu sector/Legends|Indrexu sector]] out of the Hegemony's territory beyond [[Kanaver]]. The worlds of the [[Far Perlemian]] were of little interest to the Republic during its final years, and [[Slaver/Legends|slavers]], [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] and Separatists often had free reign there. The Indrexu sector — a name that recalled the [[Indrexu Confederation]], a successor state of [[Xim's empire]] millennia before — was carved out of the Hegemony in an effort to keep the restive Indrexu worlds from making common cause with their Livien neighbors.

The [[Keldrath sector/Legends|Keldrath sector]] was another attempt by the Empire to create a buffer zone, in this case between the [[Pakuuni sector/Legends|Pakuuni sector]] and the Tion. The effort was ill-researched and backfired — that part of the Tion Hegemony had always gravitated to [[Pakuuni/Legends|Pakuuni]], and the new sector immediately fell under its neighbor's sway.

The [[Thanium sector/Legends|Thanium Worlds]] were conquered by the Tionese during [[Xim's Expansionist Period]] and formed the industrial engine of his empire, once stretching to the edges of the [[Radama Void/Legends|Radama Void]] and including worlds later known as part of the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] and the [[Gordian Reach/Legends|Gordian Reach]]. The northern, rimward portions of the Thanium Worlds were known in Xim's time as the [[Far Indrexu]]. Despite the name, the passage of millennia meant that the Thanium Worlds bore little resemblance to what they had been in Xim's time.
